cells.tense: The method is here and it is holding the work steady right now.
cells.ask: Close out one finished thing today without adding to it — then leave the desk for ten minutes before you start the next.
cells.core: The making has been given its full measure — nothing in it is still a draft to you. You close things out, sign them off, set them down, and the setting down is not defeat. What you make is exact, and part of that exactness is knowing where the edge of it is.\n\nThat is quiet, and it's the part you don't narrate to anyone. The work holds because you finished it, not because you're still carrying it. Nothing in the completion is an ending pressed against your will; it is simply the gate to the next becoming opening. You're allowed to cross it without a backward glance — you already checked it twice.
cells.sheetLine: You finish things, and the finishing doesn't cost you. It opens.
cells.verb: working through the method until it holds
cells.place: where finished work is let go of

cells.tense: You are pushing the method past the finish, rehearsing a completion that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Take one thing you're holding open and declare it done before it's perfect — say the sentence out loud, once.
cells.core: The method, in plenitude, becomes the warden of its own king. You keep the lines open, revising what has already closed, testing a version of finished that hasn't arrived so it can be signed off correctly. In this moment there's a checkpoint ahead where the thing will finally be beyond criticism, and you're living there — so what you have in hand doesn't get to count.\n\nThe rigorous clarity that is the whole point of you is being spent on surveillance now instead of release. Letting it go won't undo the work. It only says the work was real enough to release without you standing guard over its future life. That's what the next thing needs from you — hands free.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding finished work against a future it doesn't have.
cells.verb: working through the method until it holds
cells.place: where finished work is let go of

cells.tense: You left the method at an earlier door and are waiting there with the finished work.
cells.ask: Hand one finished piece to one person today — say 'that's done' — and let their response stand without reworking the thing.
cells.core: The making happened. The closing didn't. There was a door already behind you — a point where the work was actually finished — and you are waiting on the near side of it with the work held open, testing whether the result was fair to what you put in. There's no ground out there that says you gave it the right weight; you've been checking, and the gate has stayed shut.\n\nWhat the practice is missing is the small fairness of taking the work as done: your effort counted, and so did what it made. The old test isn't wrong for what it did. It's just become the place you wait instead of the place you leave. Something you made is complete, and it is waiting for you to say so before it can travel.
cells.sheetLine: The making finished. The letting-go is still at the gate.
cells.verb: working through the method until it holds
cells.place: where finished work is let go of

cells.tense: The method is already closing things out here, and you are describing it as though output happened by itself.
cells.ask: Name one thing you finished this week and say plainly it was your work — then write down what that completion freed you to look at next.
cells.core: You've been running the closing down through the work without noticing you're the one holding the pen — judging when a piece is complete, which drafts are spent, what compact belongs in the next thing. The evidence of finished making is already here. Your account of it gives the work its own engine and leaves you standing nearby.\n\nThere's a lighter question sitting behind that story and you've been skipping it: not whether this is done, but what you actually imagine coming next. That lens is the kindest tool you own. Picking it up costs nothing and gives the finished thing its proper place — and you yours.
cells.sheetLine: You already close the work. Saying so is the part you skip.
cells.verb: working through the method until it holds
cells.place: where finished work is let go of

A reader could fairly say the drawing only shows what the card is, not what it is doing in their week — so nothing below rests on that claim.
